Following observations are relevant in the context: "40.General principles relating to compensation in injury cases 5. The provision of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ("the Act", for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident. The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. The court or the Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable. A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury. This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned. [See C.K. Subramania Iyer v. T. Kunhikuttan Nair [(1969) 3 SCC 64 : AIR 1970 SC 376] , R.D. Hattangadi v. Pest Control (India) (P) Ltd. [(1995) 1 SCC 551 : 1995 SCC (Cri) 250] and Baker v. Willoughby [1970 AC 467 : (1970) 2 WLR 50 : (1969) 3 All ER 1528 (HL)] .] 6. The heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following: Pecuniary damages (Special damages) (i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalisation, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure. (ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising: (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment; (b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability. (iii) Future medical expenses. MACT No. 623/2017 Ashish Kumar Sinha Vs. Raj Kumar Sharma & Ors. Page No. 12 o Non-pecuniary damages (General damages) (iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries. (v) Loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage). (vi) Loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity). In routine personal injury cases, compensation will be awarded only under heads (i), (ii)(a) and (iv). It is only in serious cases of injury, where there is specific medical evidence corroborating the evidence of the claimant, that compensation will be granted under any of the heads (ii)(b), (iii), (v) and (vi) relating to loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability, future medical expenses, loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage) and loss of expectation of life. 7. Assessment of pecuniary damages under Item (i) and under Item (ii)(a) do not pose much difficulty as they involve reimbursement of actuals and are easily ascertainable from the evidence. Award under the head of future medical expenses--Item Ashish Kumar Sinha vs Raj Kumar Sharma on 17 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/64605767/ 8 (iii)--depends upon specific medical evidence regarding need for further treatment and cost thereof. Assessment of non-pecuniary damages--Items (iv), (v) and (vi)--involves determination of lump sum amounts with reference to circumstances such as age, nature of injury/deprivation/ disability suffered by the claimant and the effect thereof on the future life of the claimant. 26. It is settled proposition of law as held in catena of judgments that "just compensation" should include all elements that would go to place the victim in as near a position as she or he was in, before the occurrence of the accident. Whilst no amount of money or other material compensation can erase the trauma, pain and suffering that a victim undergoes after a serious accident, (or replace the loss of a loved one), monetary compensation is the manner known to law, whereby society assures some measure of restitution to those who survive, and the victims who have to face their lives. 27. texts.facts: 1. In this case, a claim petition was filed on 15.07.2017 by Sh. Ashish Kumar Sinha (hereinafter referred as claimant) who got injured in an accident which took place on 11.11.2016 at about 05.00 Pm due to rash and negligent driving of bus bearing Reg. No. Up 16At 6816 (hereinafter referred as offending vehicle) which was driven by its driver Satish (hereinafter referred as Mact No. 623/2017 Ashish Kumar Sinha Vs. Raj Kumar Sharma & Ors. Page R-2), owned by Sh. Raj Kumar Sharma (hereinafter referred as R-1) and insured with The United India Insurance Company Limited (hereinafter referred as R-3) u/s 166 r/w Sec. 140 of Mv Act seeking compensation for an amount of Rs. 5 lakhs along with interest at the rate of 12% per annum. Brief Facts: 2. On 11.11.2016, while claimant was commuting on a two wheeler bearing Reg. No. MP 09ST 9531 with his friend Gunjesh Kumar as pillion rider from his place of work at Okhla to his house at Ghaziabad, at about 07.00 pm, at Nursery Tiraha, Sec. 18, Noida, Uttar Pradesh (hereinafter called the spot of accident), a bus bearing Registration No. UP 16AT 6816 (hereinafter called the offending vehicle) came speedily from the back side and hit the scooter from behind due to which claimant fell down and sustained injuries. Both the injured persons were rushed to Max Hospital Noida. Subsequently, the information about the accident was given to the concerned police station on 16.11.2016 and present case FIR was registered on 18.11.2016 under relevant provisions of law. Investigation were undertaken. Injury has been medically opined to be simple in nature. Certified copy of charge sheet were subsequently filed in the connected criminal matter pertaining to the same accident wherein driver Satish has been charge sheeted for commission of offence punishable u/s 279/337/427 IPC. Copy of site plan, copy of insurance policy, copy of DL and other relevant documents pertaining to the accident were filed as part of charge sheet. Proceedings: 3. Notice of the claim petition was directed to be issued to respondents. Respondent no. 1 as well as Respondent no.3 were duly served and appeared before the Court whereas petition was dismissed qua Respondent no.2 for Ashish Kumar Sinha vs Raj Kumar Sharma on 17 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/64605767/ 2 failure of claimant to take steps vide order dated 18.01.2018. Written Statement MACT No. 623/2017 Ashish Kumar Sinha Vs. Raj Kumar Sharma & Ors . Page No. 3 of 26 filed on behalf of R-1/ owner as well as R-3/ Insurance Company. Reply: 4. In the Written Statement/ Reply filed on behalf of R-1, he admitted himself to be owner of offending vehicle. He generally denied the contents of claim petition. He stated that the allegations leveled against him are false and that accident happened on account of rash and negligent driving of the driver of scooter bearing Reg. No. MP 09ST 9531 and that this claim petition has been filed to extract compensation wrongfully. 5. In the WS filed on behalf of R-3/ Insurance Company, it is stated that scooterist was himself negligent in causing the accident. General defences have been taken. OPP. 3) Relief. Page No. 4 of Ex.PW1/A. He also relied upon following documents: a) Ex.PW1/1- Certified copy of FIR, certified copy of site plan, certified copy of report U/s 173 Cr.PC. b) Ex.PW1/2- Photocopy of DL of injured / petitioner same is de-exhibited being photocopy and marked as Mark A c) Ex.PW1/3- Original copy of OPD and requisition slip and medical bills. d) Mark B- Photocopy of appointment letter and salary slip. 8. PW-1 was put to cross examination by counsel for insurance company whereas none appeared on behalf of R-1 for such cross examination. of PW-2 Sh. Atul Kumar Jha, senior Executive Hospital Operation, Max Multi Specialty Noida appeared as summoned witness and was examined who was put to cross examination by counsel for insurance company, whereas none appeared on behalf of R-1 for his cross examination. 9. Upon request, PE was closed vide order dated 02.11.2022. None appeared on behalf of Respondent No. 1 to lead evidence. 10. R-3 Insurance company produced Sh. Satya Pal Singh, Assistant Manager as R3W1 and tendered evidentiary affidavit Ex.R3W1/A and relied upon Ashish Kumar Sinha vs Raj Kumar Sharma on 17 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/64605767/ 3 attested copy of police as Ex.R3W1/1, notice u/O XII Rule 8 CPC as Ex.R3W1/2 and Postal Receipt as Ex.R3W1/3. He was not cross examined by counsel for the claimant. RE was closed vide order dated 12.01.2023. Arguments: 11. Final Arguments were advanced. Written Arguments were filed on behalf of claimant, R-1/ owner as well as Insurance Company. In the written arguments filed on behalf of claimant, it is stated that the claimant was employed as Assistant Manager in a company drawing a salary of more than Rs. 65,000/- per month on the date of accident. It is argued that the claimant was in good health MACT No. 623/2017 Ashish Kumar Sinha Vs. Raj Kumar Sharma & Ors. Page No. 5 of 26 prior to the accident but has not been able to concentrate on his work post accident and has incurred huge expenses on his treatment . It is also stressed that the accident was caused solely due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle and fair compensation must be awarded in his favour with liability jointly and severally upon R-1 & R-3. 12. In Written Arguments of Respondent no.1, his liability to pay the compensation amount was denied. It is stated that any such accident never took place and that Respondent No.2 was in a stationary vehicle, rather accident took place on account of negligent driving of the two-wheeler. 13. R-3 Insurance Company has enclosed he computations at Rs. 89,000/- arguing that the owner of offending vehicle was not holding valid permit for plying his vehicle in the State of UP at the time of accident and therefore, he has violated the terms and conditions of the policy, thus, Insurance Company has no liability to pay the claimant against liability of R-1.
